pr.title: coverage: Defer part of counter-creation until codegen
pr.description:
Follow-up to #135481 and #135873.

One of the pleasant properties of the new counter-assignment algorithm is that we can stop partway through the process, store the intermediate state in MIR, and then resume the rest of the algorithm during codegen. This lets it take into account which parts of the control-flow graph were eliminated by MIR opts, resulting in fewer physical counters and simpler counter expressions.

Those improvements end up completely obsoleting much larger chunks of code that were previously responsible for cleaning up the coverage metadata after MIR opts, while also doing a more thorough cleanup job.

(That change also unlocks some further simplifications that I've kept out of this PR to limit its scope.)
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: PR 136053 is a coverage-metadata optimization, not a miscompilation fix. The replaced (historical) transformation produced post-MIR-opt mappings retaining zero operands and old numbering, e.g. `Code(Expression(0, Sub)) = (cN - Zero)` and `num_counters_after_mir_opts()`; the new transformation simplifies to `Code(Counter(N))`, filters eliminated BCBs (count zero), and compacts counter IDs. Crucially, `(cN - Zero)` and `cN` are numerically identical for every input, and renumbering counter IDs does not change any block's execution count. The only observable differences are the size/contents of the coverage expression table, the physical counter indices, and cov-map text — none of which affect the instrumented function's runtime return value or any value Miri can observe. No concrete input can make the original and transformed functions produce different defined numeric/boolean/character values while both pass Miri with O0/O3 agreement. Encoding "number of expressions" or "raw counter ID" as a return value would manufacture an artifact rather than demonstrate a semantic break. Hence no source-grounded counterexample pair exists for this metadata-only optimization.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `InstrumentCoverage` created the complete mapping from coverage-graph nodes to concrete `CovTerm`s before MIR optimizations: it ran counter creation end-to-end, injected `CounterIncrement { id }` / `ExpressionUsed { id }` statements, and stored `MappingKind::Code(CovTerm)` (and branch/MC/DC term variants) in `FunctionCoverageInfo`. After MIR opts, the `coverage_ids_info` query scanned the surviving statements into `counters_seen`/`expressions_seen`, then `identify_zero_expressions` propagated `CovTerm::Zero` through the expression graph. Codegen used `num_counters_after_mir_opts()` and replaced removed terms with zero while retaining the original expression structure. The PR description says it wanted to "stop partway through the process, store the intermediate state in MIR, and then resume the rest of the algorithm during codegen."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically replaced transformation was the post-MIR-opt zero-cleanup: removed counters/expressions were rewritten to `CovTerm::Zero` but their expression nodes and old counter numbering were retained, producing mappings such as `Code(Expression(0, Sub))` with `= (c3 - Zero)` instead of simplifying back to `Code(Counter(3))`, and using `num_counters_after_mir_opts()` (max surviving counter ID + 1) rather than a compacted count. The PR instead stores `node_flow_data`, `priority_list`, and BCB-based `MappingKind`s, then during codegen scans final MIR for surviving `VirtualCounter { bcb }` statements, computes `bcb_needs_counter` from mappings, and runs `make_node_counters` plus `transcribe_counters`. In that new transformation, a mapped BCB whose `VirtualCounter` did not survive must become `CovTerm::Zero`; unseen BCBs appearing in another node's `counter_terms` must be filtered out of the positive/negative lists, and if no positive term remains the result must be `CovTerm::Zero`, not a fallback physical counter.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` (optionally branch/MC/DC coverage) whose coverage graph has BCBs that MIR optimizations later eliminate. Historical regression inputs include `assert_not`, `bad_counter_ids`, `fn_sig_into_try`, `inline-dead` closures, `loops_branches`, `no_spans_if_not`, and `tight_inf_loop`. These are functions where a constant condition, `assert!`, `?`/try path, dead inline closure body, loop edge, or unreachable block removes the block/`VirtualCounter` that a mapping or counter expression refers to. The domain also includes unused functions, where all counters must be emitted as zero, but that is separate from BCB elimination.
analysis.summary: Coverage counter creation is split across `InstrumentCoverage` and codegen: mappings and VirtualCounter statements reference BCBs, and `coverage_ids_info` resumes counter creation after MIR opts. The key invariant is that any BCB removed by MIR opts has execution count zero and must not receive a physical counter or survive as a nonzero expression operand.
analysis.trigger: After `InstrumentCoverage`, MIR optimizations remove a BCB's leader block (and therefore its injected `VirtualCounter { bcb }`), while that BCB is still referenced by a `Code`/`Branch`/`MCDCBranch` mapping or appears in another BCB's counter-expression terms. The `coverage_ids_info` query then sees that BCB in the stored `priority_list`/`node_flow_data` but not in the final MIR `bcbs_seen` set.
preconditions: The crate is compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` (and branch/MC/DC options if branch mappings are involved).
`InstrumentCoverage` has stored BCB-based mappings plus `node_flow_data` and `priority_list` in `FunctionCoverageInfo`, and injected `CoverageKind::VirtualCounter { bcb }` into each BCB leader block.
MIR opts (including the cleanup after borrowck) eliminate at least one BCB/VirtualCounter before the `coverage_ids_info` query runs.
`coverage_ids_info` reconstructs counters from the stored graph data and the set of BCBs still present in final MIR.
Codegen resolves every mapping's BCB via `ids_info.term_for_bcb[bcb]` and only emits `llvm.instrprof.increment` when `phys_counter_for_node` contains that BCB.
pitfalls: Do not treat a BCB missing from final MIR as having a nonzero execution count; `transcribe_counters` must assign `CovTerm::Zero` to it and filter it out of other nodes' counter-term lists.
Do not leave a mapped-but-eliminated BCB without a term in `term_for_bcb`; codegen expects every BCB in a mapping to have a term and will panic otherwise.
Do not restore the old fallback that creates a physical counter when the filtered positive-term list is empty; the new code uses `unwrap_or(CovTerm::Zero)`.
Do not confuse marker cleanup with counter cleanup: `CleanupPostBorrowck` removes `BlockMarker`/`SpanMarker`, but `VirtualCounter` must be retained so codegen can still recognize surviving BCBs.
Do not derive `num_counters` from the highest surviving/old counter ID; the query now returns `next_counter_id.as_u32()` after compact counter creation.
The old `(cN - Zero)` form is semantically similar but is exactly the suboptimal output this PR removes; tests distinguish it from the simplified `Code(Counter(N))` form.
An unused function zeroing all counters via `covfun.is_used` is a separate condition from a BCB whose code was removed by MIR opts.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the coverage-map regression corpus under `tests/coverage/*.cov-map`, compiling with `-Cinstrument-coverage` and branch options where relevant. Inspect `Number of expressions`, each `Code(...)`/`Branch {...}` mapping, and `Highest counter ID seen`: a function whose dead BCB was eliminated should show no `(cN - Zero)` expression and no extra expression entry, while every surviving span still has a valid counter/zero term. For a focused pair, keep two programs identical except for a condition that makes a coverage-relevant branch compile-time dead, and compare the resulting coverage maps; the dead-BCB version must simplify its mapping and counter expression rather than retaining a zero operand. Add MIR-opt checks (`//@ test-mir-pass: InstrumentCoverage`, `-Cinstrument-coverage -Zcoverage-options=branch -Zno-profiler-runtime`) asserting `Coverage::VirtualCounter(bcbN)` is injected for graph nodes, and use the `CleanupPostBorrowck` diff to assert `BlockMarker`/`SpanMarker` are gone while `VirtualCounter` survives. Include the historical edge cases `assert_not`, `fn_sig_into_try`, `inline-dead`, `loops_branches`, `no_spans_if_not`, and `tight_inf_loop` to cover mapped BCBs eliminated by opts.
